recommendations.why: Adds the change from a set number of rows earlier in the field's own units, such as orders this month minus last month. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: you want the change relative to the earlier value
you want each period's change from the one before as a decoration on the result

recommendations.why: Ranks rows within each partition in the chosen order; rows with equal values share a rank and the next follows on: 1, 2, 2, 3. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the rank should skip past equal values, as in sports standings
every row needs its own number even when values are equal

recommendations.why: Adds the change from a set number of rows earlier as a fraction of the earlier value: 0.05 is a 5% rise on last month. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the earlier value can be 0, near 0 or negative, or the field is itself a percentage
you want the same year-ago period as the comparison
you want each period as an index value against the one before

recommendations.why: Ranks rows within each partition in the chosen order; rows with equal values share a rank and the next skips: 1, 2, 2, 4. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: equal values should share a rank with no gap after them
every row needs its own number even when values are equal
you want each record's position as a percentage of all records

recommendations.why: Adds to every row its percentile rank, rank / n * 100: the share of rows at or below it when values are untied. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: you want the value at a chosen percentile, such as the 90th
you want ranks within partitions, or tied values to share a rank
you want rows split into equal-sized bands

recommendations.why: Checks whether a numeric field's average differs from a target value, or between two groups (Welch's version). Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the same subjects are measured twice, such as before and after
two groups are compared and the measure is heavily skewed, has extreme values or is only ordered
there are three or more groups
the outcome is a yes/no rate rather than a numeric measure
the request is always a two-group comparison and should say so by name
both groups are large and reporting conventions call for a z-test

recommendations.why: Adds to every row its T-score: the z-score rescaled so the mean is 50 and one standard deviation is 10. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: you want plain standard-deviation units centred on 0
you want each row's percentile rank (the share at or below it when values are untied)

recommendations.why: Adds to every row its z-score: how many standard deviations the row's value sits above or below the mean. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: you want the centre and spread of each group, not a score per row
the field is skewed or has extreme values and you want a position they cannot distort
you want each group's value against all groups

recommendations.why: Adds to every row the value a straight-line model predicts for its target from its predictors. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: you want the coefficients, R-squared and p-values of the model
you want how far each row sits from its prediction
the target is yes/no or a count

recommendations.why: Adds to every row its residual: the actual target value minus the value a straight-line model predicts for it. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: you want the model's summary (coefficients, R-squared)
you want how unusual each row's predictor values are
you want how far a value is from the mean, with no model
